newsitem.title: USA: "Star Wars" remains a force at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Star Wars" remains a force at U.S. box office.

text.p: Almost 20 years after it helped usher in the age of the special effects blockbuster, "Star Wars" returned to the big screen at the weekend and earned a stunning $36.2 million, according to studio estimates.

The sci-fi extravaganza, which is being re-released with 4-1/2 minutes of extra footage, easily topped the box office listings, and now stands as the second-highest grossing film at the domestic box office with $358.9 million.
Exhibitor Relations, which collects the studio estimates, said the Friday to Sunday total was the ninth-highest three-day opener and the top January opener.
"We were bullish, but nobody was this bullish," said Tom Sherak, chairman of 20th Domestic Film Group, a unit of News Corp. -owned 20th Century Fox which released the film.
The highest grossing film at the domestic box office is "E.T. The Extraterrestial" with $399.8 million, and the previous number two was "Jurassic Park" with $357.1 million.
"Star Wars," in which Luke Skywalker, Han Solo and Princess Leia battle Darth Vader and his stormtroopers on the Death Star, earned an average of $17,200 from 2,104 screens.

This is in sharp contrast to the film's performance first time around when it opened quietly on 32 screens on May 25, 1977 -- a Wednesday -- and ended up with a then-resounding $2.6 million after its first six days.
In addition to the extra footage, the re-release boasts better sound and digital effects, all at a reported cost of $10 million.

Sherak said the re-release played to packed houses, with 50 percent of the audience aged 25 and under. The other half, he said, "are there for the celebration. They're re-living 1977 again with their families."
Post-screening polls of young males showed that 96 percent rated the film excellent or very good, Sherak said.

The two "Star Wars" sequels have also been spruced up and will be released imminently in order to set the scene for three new movies in the cycle. "Star Wars" creator George Lucas is set to begin filming the first of three "prequels" from his own screenplay next fall. The next two will probably be written and directed by hired hands working from Lucas' notes. These three are scheduled to be released in May 1999, 2001 and 2003.

In the meantime, "The Empire Strikes Back" (domestic gross $222.7 million) will be re-released on Feb. 21, followed by "Return Of The Jedi" ($263.7 million) on March 7. "Star Wars" will be able to add to its international total of $215.7 million beginning next month.

The only other new entry in the top 10 was "Gridlock'd," starring Tim Roth and late rapper Tupac Shakur as junkies who encounter bureaucratic hurdles as they try to kick their habit. It opened in ninth with $2.8 million from 745 screens, for a modest average of $3,785 per screen. The film is released by Gramercy Pictures, a unit of PolyGram NV..

The number two and three spots went to the two holiday hits that show no sign of losing momentum. "Jerry Maguire," which was first last weekend, earned $5.6 million at the weekend as its total rose to $117 million. Third place went to the spoof horror "Scream" with $4.8 million. Its total now stands at $70.6 million.
"Jerry Maguire" is released by TriStar Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp. "Scream" is released by Miramax Films, a unit of Walt Disney Co.
